title: Keep the archive reader's connection pool full

blocks.text: The billing importer reads the first record of each meter archive from the archive store, over a pool of a few connections. `ArchiveReader.Decoder` checks an archive's header when it is constructed, and closing a decoder closes the connection under it, the way a stream decorator closes the stream it wraps.

Two things went wrong last month. A partner uploaded a few hundred CSV exports instead of archives, and from then on every import failed with `pool exhausted`. And on an ordinary day, two imports were found reading over the same connection at once.

Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/ArchiveReader.java`: `firstRecord(...)` and `Lease.close()`. When you're done, a rejected file costs the pool nothing, and a connection is never handed to two readers. About six lines in total.

cases.says: the first record of a valid archive is returned, read after read, from a pool of one connection
a file the decoder rejects while being constructed still leaves its connection back in the pool
after a read, the pool hands its connections to two borrowers as two different connections

origin.section: Only a Resource That Finished Constructing Is Closed, So Declare Each Stream Separately

concepts: Declared separately, a wrapped resource is closed twice; Closeable requires that to be harmless, AutoCloseable does not, so a close() of your own must be idempotent.
Only a resource that finished constructing is closed, so a stream created inside another resource's constructor call leaks when that constructor throws; declaring each stream separately closes it.
